headline: Predictive structure models repurposed for generative binder and ligand design
label: Generative Molecular Design Models
summary: Recent preprints report all-atom predictors and pocket co-design models being inverted or RL-aligned to generate binders, not only to predict them.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the reuse of predictive all-atom models as generative engines. DREAM inverts the frozen Boltz-2 predictor through Geometric Score Distillation to design cyclic peptide binders, selecting from up to 55 residue types. PocketX applies online Group Relative Policy Optimization to align a ligand-conditioned pocket co-design model with binding and developability objectives. SeedProteo, a diffusion-based model, targets de novo all-atom design and is benchmarked on unconditional generation and binder design. What is new relative to the predictive work is the shift from scoring structures toward generation and optimization under explicit objectives. Other items, including SeedFold, FlashAffinity, ProtBFF, and BindMecNet, remain predictive structure or affinity models and do not share this framing.
